# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

## I. By Primary Task Type

### A. Loop/Path Drawing
Puzzles where the solver draws a single continuous loop or path through the grid.

#### A1. Pure Loop Construction
- **Masyu** – Loop through cells with black/white circle constraints on turning/straight behavior
- **Slitherlink** – Loop on grid edges/dots with numeric constraints on surrounding line segments
- **Mid-loop** – Loop through cells where black circles must be midpoints of straight segments
- **Nagareru** – Directional loop with wind constraints affecting movement
- **Moon-or-Sun** – Loop through rooms alternating between moon and sun symbols
- **Dotchi-Loop** – Loop through cells with per-region constraints on circle behavior (all straight or all turning)
- **Suraromu** – Loop starting/ending at numbered circle, passing through all gates in specified order

#### A2. Loop with Shading
- **Yajilin** – Loop construction combined with placing black cells; arrow clues indicate black cell counts

#### A3. Path/Line Connection
- **Numberlink** – Connect pairs of identical numbers with non-crossing paths
- **Hashiwokakero** – Connect island nodes with bridges (1 or 2) to form a connected network
- **Pencils** – Draw lines from pencil tips through cells, with length constraints

---

### B. Cell Shading/Painting
Puzzles where the solver colors certain cells black (or leaves them white).

#### B1. Shading with Numeric Clues (clue cells remain unshaded)
- **Nurikabe** – Numbers define white island sizes; black cells form one connected wall with no 2×2
- **Kurodoko** – Numbers indicate total visible white cells in four directions; black cells non-adjacent, whites connected
- **Kurotto** – Circle numbers indicate sum of adjacent black cell groups; circle cells stay white
- **Akari** – Place light bulbs in white cells; numbered black cells constrain adjacent bulb count; bulbs illuminate and cannot see each other
- **Shakashaka** – Place triangles in cells so remaining white areas form rectangles; numbers constrain adjacent triangle count

#### B2. Shading with Regional Constraints
- **Heyawake** – Rooms with numbers dictating shaded cell count; white cells can't span 3+ rooms in a line; shaded cells non-adjacent; whites connected
- **Norinori** – Each bold-lined region contains exactly two shaded cells; all shaded cells form dominoes
- **Nurimisaki** – Circle cells are white "promontories" (one white neighbor); numbers indicate white line length; no 2×2 of either color
- **Nuritwin** – Each region has exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; all shaded connected; no 2×2 shading; blocks in same region don't touch
- **LITS** – Each region gets one tetromino; same-shape tetrominoes can't touch (except corners); all shaded connected; no 2×2
- **Nurimeizu** – Rooms entirely shaded or white; create maze from S to G; circles on shortest path, triangles not; no 2×2 of either color
- **Sto-stone** – Numbers indicate black cell count per room; black cells don't connect across rooms; when "dropped" they fill bottom half
- **Tilepaint** – Entire tiles colored or not; diagonal-cell numbers constrain black cell counts in rows/columns
- **Usowan** – Numbers show adjacent shaded cell count, but one number per room is wrong; shaded non-adjacent; whites connected

#### B3. Shading to Form Specific Shapes
- **Choco Banana** – Black groups must form rectangles/squares; white groups must NOT form rectangles/squares; numbers indicate area size
- **Chained Block** – Black cell groups ("blocks") with size numbers; blocks chain at corners; unique shapes per chain

#### B4. Shading by Elimination
- **Hitori** – Shade duplicate numbers so no number repeats in any row/column; shaded cells non-adjacent; whites connected

---

### C. Region Division/Partitioning
Puzzles where the solver divides the grid into regions or blocks.

#### C1. Rectangular Partitioning
- **Shikaku** – Divide grid into rectangles; each contains exactly one number equal to its area

#### C2. Fixed-Size Partitioning
- **Five Cells** – Divide grid into pentomino-shaped blocks; numbers indicate surrounding block boundary lines

#### C3. Shape-Constrained Partitioning
- **Sashigane** – Divide grid into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends; arrows mark ends pointing toward bends; numbers indicate block size
- **Double Choco** – Divide into blocks where each block has matching white and gray sub-regions of identical shape

#### C4. Number-Based Partitioning
- **Fillomino** – Fill grid with numbers; groups of same number form blocks of that size; same-sized blocks can't be adjacent

---

### D. Number/Symbol Placement
Puzzles where the solver fills cells with numbers or symbols.

#### D1. Latin Square Variants
- **Sudoku** – Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 box

#### D2. Regional Number Filling
- **Ripple Effect** – Each room gets consecutive numbers from 1; same numbers in a row/column must be spaced apart by at least that number's value
- **Makaro** – Each room gets 1 to N (room size); arrow cells point to the largest neighbor; same numbers can't be adjacent across rooms
- **Nansuke** – Fill blank cells with digits to place all listed multi-digit numbers in crossword fashion

#### D3. Symbol Placement
- **Juosan** – Fill every cell with — or |; territory numbers constrain the difference; runs of — limited vertically, runs of | limited horizontally

#### D4. Sequence Placement
- **Hebi** – Place snakes (numbered 1–5) in white cells; snakes can't touch; line-of-sight constraints from snake heads

---

### E. Object Movement/Placement
Puzzles where the solver moves or places objects.

- **Satogaeri** – Move numbered circles within countries so each country has exactly one; circles move specified distances without crossing paths
- **Yosenabe** – Move all circles into gray areas via straight arrows; arrows don't cross; gray area numbers equal sum of entering circles
- **Evolomino** – Place growing polyomino blocks along arrow paths; each subsequent block adds one square to the previous shape

---

## II. By Constraint Mechanisms

### Connectivity Constraints
*White/unshaded cells must form a connected network:*
Hitori, Heyawake, Kurodoko, Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Usowan, Yajilin

*Shaded cells must form a connected network:*
LITS, Nuritwin, Nurikabe (black wall)

### Adjacency Prohibition
*Shaded cells cannot be orthogonally adjacent:*
Hitori, Heyawake, Usowan, Yajilin, Kurodoko

### 2×2 Prohibition
*No 2×2 square of same color:*
Nurikabe, LITS, Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu, Sto-stone, Nuritwin

### Visibility/Line-of-Sight Clues
*Numbers count visible cells or objects in cardinal directions:*
Akari, Kurodoko, Yajilin, Nurimisaki, Pencils

### Room/Region-Based Constraints
*Bold-lined regions impose local rules:*
Heyawake, Norinori, Double Choco, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Nurimeizu, Sto-stone, Nuritwin, Usowan, Five Cells, Suraromu

---

## III. By Grid Element Type

| Element | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Numbered black cells** | Akari, Shakashaka, Yajilin, Hebi |
| **Circled numbers** | Kurodoko, Kurotto, Hashiwokakero, Satogaeri, Nurimisaki, Yosenabe |
| **Black/white circle tokens** | Masyu, Dotchi-Loop, Mid-loop |
| **Bold-lined rooms** | Heyawake, Norinori, Double Choco, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Moon-or-Sun, Suraromu, Nurimeizu, Sto-stone, Nuritwin, Usowan, Five Cells, Dotchi-Loop |
| **Arrows** | Makaro, Sashigane, Yajilin, Hebi, Nagareru, Evolomino, Yosenabe |
| **Dots on grid intersections** | Slitherlink |
| **Pre-filled numbers** | Sudoku, Hitori, Fillomino, Nansuke, Ripple Effect |
| **Colored/gray regions** | Double Choco, Sto-stone, Yosenabe |
| **Moon/Sun symbols** | Moon-or-Sun |
| **Gates (dotted lines)** | Suraromu |
